featureRef: 29.6 Pickup notification by scanned barcode at the gate
name: Let a guardian with no card and no location raise the request by scanning a barcode displayed at the gate
priorityReason: Without it a guardian who refused location permission and holds no card has no route but the desk.

goal.capability: to raise the collection request by scanning the barcode at the gate from my own portal
goal.outcome: I can tell the office I am here even with no card and no location

secondaryActors.involvement: Displays the barcode and controls its rotation.

additional.description: A guardian scans the barcode displayed at the gate from their portal (BR-2).

preconditions.condition: A barcode is displayed at the gate for the branch (BR-1).
The guardian is signed in to their portal.
The guardian's children are enrolled at that branch.

establishedBy.name: View and maintain the student record

preconditions.condition: The guardian holds no open pickup request (BR-4).

postConditions: A barcode was displayed at the gate for the branch, and the School Admin controlled its rotation.
The guardian scanned it from their own portal while signed in.
The portal asked whether they were here to collect and which of their children.
A request was raised on confirmation, exactly as by geofence, and appeared in the pickup queue.
A request was refused where the guardian already held an open one.
This route served a guardian who holds no card and whose location is not available, and who would otherwise have had to go to the desk.
The record shows how the request was raised, and identifies nobody.

businessRules.rule: A barcode is displayed at the gate for the branch. The School Admin displays it and controls its rotation.
A guardian signed in to their portal scans it. Without the sign-in the scan does nothing, since the portal is what identifies the family.

The portal asks whether they are here to collect and which of their children, and on confirmation a request is raised exactly as by geofence, appearing in the pickup queue. Scanning alone raises nothing.
A request is refused where the guardian already holds an open one, and the existing request is shown.
This route exists for a guardian who has no pickup card and whose location is not available. Without it they have no route but the desk.
The barcode is rotated, so one photographed once and kept does not work indefinitely.
This route, the card and the geofence are all means of raising a request rather than checks on a person. The record shows how the request was raised and identifies nobody.
A barcode from another branch does not raise a request at this one.
Where a child named is not enrolled at that branch, they are not offered.

basicFlow.userAction: Displays the barcode at the gate for the branch and sets how often it rotates.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Publishes the barcode and rotates it on the schedule set.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Portal → Scan the gate barcode
basicFlow.userAction: Scans the barcode displayed at the gate from their own portal.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the barcode belongs to that branch. Without the sign-in the scan does nothing.

basicFlow.navigation: Scan the gate barcode → Select the children
basicFlow.systemResponse: Asks whether they are here to collect and which of their children.

basicFlow.userAction: Confirms they are here, and names the children.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Raises the request on the confirmation. Scanning alone raises nothing.
Records the request exactly as by geofence and puts it in the pickup queue.
Refuses a second request and shows the existing one where the guardian already holds one open.

The scan does nothing without a signed-in portal session, since the barcode itself identifies the gate and not the family.

openQuestions.question: How often should the barcode rotate? Rotating too rarely makes a photograph a permanent key, and too often means a printed sheet at the gate is always stale.
openQuestions.assumption: Configurable as modelled, defaulting to daily. The school's choice is not stated.

openQuestions.question: No feature creates gates, and a branch may have more than one.
Can a guardian scan the barcode from outside the school, from a photograph somebody sent them?
openQuestions.assumption: Yes as modelled, since nothing checks location on this route. The rotation is the only limit.

openQuestions.question: Is the barcode displayed on a screen or printed, and who reprints it after a rotation?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.
